text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Scandinavian Airlines(SAS) and Denmark's Maersk Air have lodged a complaint with the European Commission, expressing fears of the consequences of opposition to the merger between U.S. Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas on the grounds that such a move would lead to higher aircraft and ticket prices in Europe.

--At the EU foreign minister meeting in Brussels, only Italy gave full support for Denmark's call for simultaneous membership negotiations with all 10 interested eastern European applicants and not just five as the EU Commission recommends.
--Danish export industries can expect major advances in 1997 and 1998 since the crown currency has slipped four percent in value in the past six months, a new analysis shows.

--The Conservative opposition party sees no risk of the incumbent Social Democrat-led centre-left coalition government falling over the 1998 state budget, due to be unveiled in draft form on August 26 for passage by parliament by Christmas. Elections are not due in Denmark until September 1998 at latest.

--A government-led committee is to be urgently summoned to explain media reports that the new metro train system connecting Copenhagen with its airport will only have a terminus at the international departure section of the airport and no direct rail link to the domestic terminal.
--Danish exports to Sweden and Britain are soaring, while Denmark is losing market shares in Germany due to lack of initiative in supplying leading export firms, says a critical German report.
